estate, enough to guide prioritization, coach the team, and get hands-on when necessary.</li> <li>A track record of driving broad, governed rollouts of security capability across an engineering organization you do not own, and sustaining adoption after launch.</li> <li>Experience translating security requirements into controls that engineering teams can meet without slowing down.</li> You'll also contribute to key areas such as the graph query engine, indexing pipelines, cloud storage integrations, and multi-tenant behavior. Through thoughtful system design, better tooling, clear runbooks, and shared context, you'll help reduce single points of failure and improve how we build, deploy, and operate the service.</p> <h2>What you’ll do</h2> <ul> <li value="1">Design, build, and operate GitLab Orbit backend services, primarily in Rust, within a distributed, cloud-native environment.</li> <li value="2">Improve the deployment, monitoring, and operations of GitLab Orbit across GitLab.com, Dedicated, and Self-Managed deployments using Kubernetes, Helm, Terraform, and cloud services from Amazon Web Services, Google Cloud Platform, or both.</li> <li value="3">Automate recurring operational work and build tools that make deployments, upgrades, recovery, capacity management, and service maintenance safer and more efficient.</li> <li value="4">Strengthen observability across application, data, orchestration, and infrastructure layers by improving metrics, logs, traces, dashboards, alerts, and service-level indicators to track availability, error rates, and incident response time while collaborating with site reliability engineering teams to improve incident response, on-call readiness, runbooks, and troubleshooting workflows.</li> <li value="5">Investigate production issues, address underlying causes, and write backend code that handles concurrency, partial failures, retries, consistency, idempotency, performance, and multi-tenant isolation.</li> <li value="6">Build and improve the graph query engine, software development lifecycle (SDLC) and code indexing pipelines, cloud storage integrations, and application programming interface (API) and Model Context Protocol (MCP) surfaces.</li> <li value="7">Design reliable, scalable, and cost-aware data workflows using systems such as Amazon Simple Storage Service (S3), ClickHouse, NATS, and Siphon.</li> <li value="8">Own changes from technical design through rollout and iteration, documenting constraints and trade-offs while collaborating asynchronously with product, data, infrastructure, security, delivery, artificial intelligence, and SRE teams.</li> </ul> <h2>What you’ll bring</h2> <ul> <li value="1">Experience designing, building, and operating production backend services with strong Rust skills or clear evidence that you can ramp up and contribute in a Rust-first, performance-sensitive codebase.</li> <li value="2">Experience with distributed-system design, including concurrency, failure handling, consistency, messaging, data partitioning, scalability, and multi-tenant isolation.</li> <li value="3">Hands-on knowledge of AWS, GCP, or both, including cloud networking, identity and access management, compute, storage, and object storage such as Amazon Simple Storage Service (S3).</li> <li value="4">Experience deploying and troubleshooting applications on Kubernetes with Helm and contributing to repeatable, reviewable infrastructure changes using Terraform or similar infrastructure as code tools.</li> <li value="5">Experience improving the reliability, observability, maintainability, and on-call readiness of backend services, and diagnosing issues across application, data, orchestration, and infrastructure layers to deliver lasting code and system improvements.</li> <li value="6">Strong system design skills, including making and explaining architectural decisions, documenting constraints, and aligning trade-offs with product and platform needs; ability to work autonomously in ambiguous environments by identifying problems, driving solutions, and taking ownership.</li> <li value="7">Ability to learn and apply new languages, tools, and frameworks as the problem requires, such as Ruby, Go, or TypeScript and Vue in adjacent parts of the stack, along with excellent written communication and asynchronous collaboration skills demonstrated through thoughtful code review, mentoring, incident communication, and context sharing.</li> </ul> <h2>About the team</h2> <p>The Orbit team sits within the Data Engineering organization and builds GitLab Orbit, the service that turns GitLab's SDLC and code data into a unified property graph. We expose it through a high-performance, ClickHouse-backed query engine and MCP tools. We're a small group of senior engineers, working closely with partners across AI, including GitLab Duo Agent Platform, analytics, infrastructure, delivery, and security because our work touches many layers of the platform.</p> <p>We work asynchronously and value strong ownership. We expect each engineer to build a deep understanding of the system and help evolve it over time. As adoption grows, we're focused on scaling the service sustainably and making it reliable and easy to deploy and operate for GitLab.com, Dedicated, and Self-Managed customers.</p><div class="content-pay-transparency"><div class="pay-input"><div class="description"><p><em>The base salary range for this role’s listed level is currently for residents of the United States only. title: Senior Product Manager, Secret Detection and Vulnerability Research
description: <div class="content-intro"><p>GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.</p> <p>The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OuZIb5zszQI">Co-create the future with us</a> as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.</p> <p>*<em>Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><h2>An overview of this role</h2> <p>As a <strong>Senior Product Manager</strong>, you will own GitLab's Secret Detection offering and the Vulnerability Research function that produces the detection content across security products. Secret Detection is one of the highest-signal, highest-volume security capabilities on the platform. Leaked credentials are the most common initial access vector in real breaches, and as AI agents write, commit, and configure more of the software, the surface area for exposed secrets grows faster than the number of humans watching it.</p> <p>You will own the full loop: detect a secret with high precision, tell the customer whether it is still live, get it revoked, and prevent the next one from ever landing. In parallel, you will own vulnerability research as a product asset rather than a back-office function. The detection rules, advisory data, and malicious package and reference intelligence your team produces are what make GitLab's security scanners worth paying for, and they need to ship on a cadence with measurable quality.</p> <p>This is an outcome-owning role - you will carry adoption, retention, and revenue targets for your area and be expected to explain how your roadmap moves them.</p> <p><strong>Some examples of our projects:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Push protection and pre-receive blocking that stops a credential before it reaches a repository, without wrecking developer flow</li> <li>Secret validity checking and automated revocation partnerships with major cloud and SaaS token issuers</li> <li>Detection content pipelines that turn threat research into shipped rules, with precision and recall tracked per rule</li> <li>Intelligence-driven detection of malicious packages, dependencies, and references entering the software supply chain</li> </ul> <h2>What you'll do</h2> <ul> <li><strong>Own</strong> the business outcomes for Secret Detection and Vulnerability Research, including adoption, expansion, competitive win rate, and revenue contribution. Bring a point of view on packaging and pricing, not just features.</li> <li><strong>Set</strong> the strategy for the full secret lifecycle: prevention, detection, validation, revocation, and reporting across GitLab.com, Dedicated, and Self-Managed.</li> <li><strong>Treat</strong> detection content as a product. Define how rules, advisories, and intelligence feeds are sourced, validated, versioned, and measured, and make quality visible to customers.</li> <li><strong>Hold</strong> the line on detection quality. False positives are a product defect and you will own the metrics that prove precision is improving.</li> <li><strong>Work</strong> at the level of the technology. Read the rule syntax, question the entropy heuristics, understand why a scanner missed something, and challenge engineering with informed alternatives.</li> <li><strong>Use</strong> AI to compress the distance between question and answer. Pull your own data, prototype your own flows, synthesize research and competitive input yourself, and bring conclusions rather than requests for someone else to investigate.</li> <li><strong>Build</strong> the case for where AI belongs in the product: triage, rule generation, remediation guidance, and reducing the human review burden per finding.</li> <li><strong>Partner</strong> with engineering, security research, threat intelligence, Field, and GitLab's own Security team, who are one of your most demanding users.</li> <li><strong>Communicate</strong> in writing, asynchronously, with enough precision that a distributed team can act without a meeting.</li> </ul> <h2>What you'll bring</h2> <ul> <li><strong>Domain depth</strong> in application security, vulnerability management, or security research. You have worked on or adjacent to scanners, detection content, threat intelligence, or SDLC security tooling and you know how these products actually get evaluated in a bake-off.</li> <li><strong>Technical credibility</strong> sufficient to earn the respect of a security engineering team. You do not need to have written the scanner, but you should be able to reason about detection logic, data pipelines, CI integration, and the tradeoffs between coverage and noise.</li> <li><strong>Commercial reasoning.</strong> You start from revenue mechanics, buyer motion, and competitive displacement, then work inward to product decisions. Candidates who reason only from feature lists outward are not a fit.</li> <li><strong>Evidence of using AI as a force multiplier</strong> in your own work: research, analysis, data pulls, prototyping, drafting. Consuming a chat assistant occasionally is not the same as restructuring how you work.</li> <li><strong>Judgment under ambiguity.</strong> You bring structured options and a recommendation instead of escalating an open question.</li> <li><strong>Bias for clarity.</strong> You can take a noisy, technical, politically contested problem and produce one page that everyone can align on.</li> <li><strong>Bonus:</strong> hands-on background as a developer, security engineer, red teamer, or researcher; experience with credential and token ecosystems; experience commercializing a data or intelligence asset.</li> </ul> <h2>About the team</h2> <p>This role sits in GitLab's Security product management organization, which owns application security testing, vulnerability management, supply chain security, secrets management, and AI governance. The Security Section is central to GitLab's Ultimate tier and to the shift toward consumption-based product revenue, so the work is visible to senior leadership and directly tied to company results. You will work asynchronously with engineering, design, and research counterparts across multiple regions, and with the Field teams who take this to market.</p><div class="content-conclusion"><h4><strong>How GitLab Supports Full-Time Employees</strong></h4> <ul> <li><a href="https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/total-rewards/benefits/general-and-entity-benefits/">Benefits to support your health, finances, and well-being</a></li> <li><a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/people-group/time-off-and-absence/time-off-types/#flexible-paid-time-off-pto">Flexible Paid Time Off </a></li> <li><a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/company/culture/inclusion/tmrg-tmag/">Team Member Resource Groups</a></li> <li><a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/total-rewards/stock-options/">Equity Compensation & Employee Stock Purchase Plan</a></li> <li><a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/people-group/learning-and-development/growth-and-development/">Growth and Development Fund</a></li> <li><a href="https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/total-rewards/benefits/general-and-entity-benefits/#parental-leave">Parental Leave</a> </li> </ul> <p>Please note that we welcome interest from candidates with varying levels of experience; many successful candidates do not meet every single requirement. GitLab SaaS, Self-Managed, and Dedicated architecture choices in light of their security and compliance requirements.</li> <li>Lead technical discovery to understand customer security, compliance, and infrastructure needs, and use that insight to guide implementation plans and deliverables.</li> <li>Lead migrations from legacy source code management and continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) tooling, including application security tools such as Snyk, Checkmarx, Veracode, SonarQube, and GitGuardian, to GitLab CI/CD and GitLab security scanners.</li> <li>Support description: <div class="content-intro"><p>GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.</p> <p>The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><h4>An overview of this role</h4> <p>Help us build the next generation of authentication services at GitLab. As a Senior Backend Engineer on the Authentication team, you'll work on authentication features across the Rails monolith and GATE, our new identity and access management control and data plane that supports every GitLab deployment model.</p> <p>In this role, you'll expand authentication mechanisms such as support for agentic identities while helping keep GitLab and its customers secure through robust access management tooling and by addressing vulnerabilities reported through our HackerOne program.</p> <p>The Authentication team works across many core components used by external users and GitLab teams. GATE will become the foundation for token issuance, validation, and identity services across GitLab.com multi-tenant SaaS, Self-Managed, Dedicated, and air-gapped environments. This means your work will have a direct impact on the GitLab product and the customers and users who rely on it.</p> <p>Some of our projects include:</p> <ul> <li value="1">Building GATE as the centralized service for token issuance and validation</li> <li value="2">Token consolidation and migration of authentication paths out of the Rails monolith</li> <li value="3">Passkeys and passwordless authentication</li> <li value="4">Composite identities to merge machine and human authorization for AI</li> <li value="5">Service accounts and secure automation improvements</li> <li value="6">Security Assertion Markup Language (SAML), Lightweight Directory Access Protocol (LDAP), OpenID Connect (OIDC), and System for Cross-domain Identity Management (SCIM) enhancements for automated user provisioning and single sign-on (SSO)</li> </ul> <h4>What you’ll do</h4> <ul> <li value="1">Contribute to the team's overall direction and play a direct part in shaping the future roadmap of GATE and GitLab's authentication services.</li> <li value="2">Design and implement authentication features across the Rails monolith and GATE, including token issuance, validation, and identity services.</li> <li value="3">Help migrate authentication and token management paths from the monolith into GATE while maintaining reliability across all deployment models.</li> <li value="4">Build authentication mechanisms from the ground up, such as Workload Identity Federation.</li> <li value="5">Bolster the security posture of our users and organizations through robust access management and by addressing vulnerabilities reported through our HackerOne program.</li> <li value="6">Solve technical problems of high scope and complexity across Go and Ruby codebases.</li> <li value="7">Help define and improve internal standards for style, maintainability, and best practices in a high-scale environment. Maintain and advocate for these standards through code review.</li> <li value="8">Represent GitLab and its values in public communication around broader initiatives, specific projects, and Roughly 400 policy classes and a YAML catalog of about 1,900 permissions sit behind every API request. You will work on the permission model itself (fine-grained token permissions, custom roles, and the GraphQL and REST surfaces that enforce them). You will also help move that model onto GitLab's next-generation authorization stack, which pairs the Rails monolith with a Rust policy engine using Zanzibar-style relationship tuples and Cedar policies. The monolith already loads that engine in-process and can reach it over gRPC.</p> <p>Some examples of our projects:</p> <ul> <li>Refactoring GitLab's policy layer so the same permission definitions can be evaluated by the monolith and by our new authorization service</li> <li>Extending fine-grained token permissions to more resources and more kinds of principal, including the service identities behind AI agents</li> </ul> <h4>What you'll do</h4> <ul> <li>Design and ship authorization changes in GitLab's Ruby on Rails monolith, where a single request can trigger hundreds of permission checks.</li> <li>Own a workstream end to end. Problem definition through feature-flagged rollout, dual-run verification, and cleanup.</li> <li>Build and extend fine-grained permissions for tokens and roles, and keep the permission catalog coherent as it grows.</li> <li>Extend and harden authorization enforcement across GraphQL and the REST API.</li> <li>Refactor long-lived policy code so both the monolith and our new authorization engine can evaluate it, without changing behavior for existing customers.</li> <li>Improve the reliability, performance, and security posture of existing authorization systems, including paying down permission-model debt.</li> <li>Partner with the authentication, platform, AI, and modular-service teams on interface contracts as authorization moves toward a shared service.</li> <li>Drive technical decisions in writing. Design docs, architecture decision records, and code review, in a fully asynchronous organization.</li> </ul> <h4>What you'll bring</h4> <ul> <li>Significant experience building and operating production Ruby on Rails applications.</li> <li>Experience designing or implementing authorization systems, including role-based access control and fine-grained permissions.</li> <li>A security mindset. You treat a permission bug as a security bug, and you reason about blast radius before elegance.</li> <li>Comfort making careful changes to large, long-lived codebases. Incremental refactors, feature-flagged rollouts, and migrations that must not change behavior for existing users.</li> <li>Working knowledge of GraphQL and API authorization patterns.</li> <li>Attention to performance at scale. You understand why one uncached check matters when it runs hundreds of times per request.</li> <li>Preferred: hands-on PostgreSQL experience.</li> <li>Strong written communication. You are effective when most decisions happen in a document or a merge request rather than a meeting.</li> <li>Helpful but not required: Rust, gRPC or Protocol Buffers, Cedar or other policy languages, Zanzibar-style authorization systems, Go, or service-oriented architecture. Several engineers on this team picked up Rust for this work and we will support you doing the same.</li> <li>We welcome transferable experience from adjacent domains such as identity, policy engines, and platform security.</li> </ul> <h4>About the team</h4> <p>The Authorization team owns the capabilities that determine what users, tokens, and automated agents can access across GitLab. Our work runs on two tracks. We are strengthening the permission model inside the Ruby on Rails monolith (fine-grained token permissions, custom roles, and the policy layer that enforces them), and we are moving that model onto a shared authorization platform built for GitLab's modular and cell-based future.</p> <p>We work closely with the teams building GitLab's authentication layer, its Rust authorization engine, and the first modular services adopting it. <li>Experience engaging with enterprise customers in technical presales, consulting, or similar roles and guiding them through solution design and evaluation.</li> <li>Proficiency across the software development lifecycle, including modern DevSecOps practices, continuous integration and continuous deployment workflows, and GitLab or comparable source control and collaboration platforms.</li> technical evaluations such as proofs of concept or proofs of value, contribute to tenders or audits, and design and run workshops or value stream assessments.</li> <li>Clear technical communication, presentation, and relationship-building skills, with the ability to adapt messages for practitioners and senior business and technical decision-makers and represent customer perspectives across Product Management, Engineering, Sales, and Marketing.</li> <li>Motivation to continue developing professionally by learning new technologies, deepening GitLab platform expertise, and applying transferable experience from related fields.</li> <li>Fluency in Korean and English.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>About the team</strong></h2> <p>The Solutions Architect team is part of GitLab's Sales teams.</li> <li>Knowledge of California enterprise market, including key industries, buying centers, and decision-making dynamics, with the ability to build and nurture a relevant professional network.</li> <li>Ability to drive new business acquisition and expansion within enterprise accounts through consultative, multi-stakeholder sales motions that lead to sustainable, long-term customer use GitLab and Salesforce in your daily work, and travel as needed while following company travel policies.</li> </ul> <h3><strong>About the team</strong></h3> <p>The Enterprise Sales team is title: Senior Support Engineer
description: <div class="content-intro"><p>GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OuZIb5zszQI">Co-create the future with us</a> as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.</p> <p>*<em>Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. You'll join the Engineering department and work directly with customers as they encounter edge cases. You'll dig into Linux systems, logs, and our Ruby on Rails codebase to troubleshoot performance issues, reproduce bugs, and contribute merge requests that fix problems at the source.</p> <p>You'll also improve our documentation, refine support processes in our issue tracker, and collaborate closely with Product, Development, Infrastructure, Customer Success, and Sales so customer feedback directly shapes our roadmap. In your first year, you'll build deep expertise across a range of GitLab implementations, strengthen our ability to keep customers productive on both self-managed GitLab and GitLab.com software as a service, and help create tools and content that make support more efficient and effective for the entire team.</p> <p>Some examples of our projects:</p> <ul> <li><a href="https://gitlab.com/gitlab-com/support/toolbox/gitlab-detective">A tool to automatically check a GitLab Omnibus install for known issues</a></li> <li><a href="https://gitlab.com/gitlab-com/support/toolbox/gitlabsos">A solution to capture the state of a customer’s server for easier troubleshooting</a></li> <li><a href="https://gitlab.com/gitlab-com/support/toolbox/sosparser">A tool which turns log files into interactive tables to easily sort and filter columns</a></li> <li><a href="https://docs.gitlab.com/ci/chatops/">A ChatOps feature that makes it easier to identify user accounts on GitLab.com</a></li> </ul> <h2><strong>What you’ll do</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Act as an escalation point for difficult customer interactions and lead the resolution of complex issues through Zendesk tickets, merge requests, email, and video calls.</li> <li>Mentor and guide teammates on complex troubleshooting and customer communication through pairing sessions and cross-team collaboration.</li> <li>Advocate for and drive improvements to support practices, product quality, and reusable documentation and support content that directly influence team objectives.</li> <li>Collaborate with Product, Development, Infrastructure, Customer Success, and Sales teams to shape product goals, roadmaps, and priorities while driving fixes and new features.</li> <li>Participate in regular weekday and weekend on-call rotations during daytime hours, providing emergency support for self-managed GitLab and software as a service customers and coordinating incident communications with the GitLab.com Production team.</li> <li>Participate in hiring by reviewing applications and assessments and joining interviews to help grow the Support team.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What you’ll bring</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Experience owning complex, customer-facing technical cases from initial contact through triage, reproduction, bug reporting, resolution, and clear customer communication, including difficult or escalated interactions.</li> <li>Strong experience with Linux systems administration, scripting, Git, and continuous integration and continuous delivery in production or customer environments, with the ability to investigate issues at both the infrastructure and application levels.</li> <li>Ability to mentor teammates on complex troubleshooting and customer communication through pairing sessions, case reviews, and cross-team collaboration.</li> <li>Experience collaborating with Product, Engineering, and Sales teams to turn customer feedback into product fixes, feature improvements, and roadmap priorities.</li> <li>Familiarity with DevOps practices and technologies such as Kubernetes and serverless computing, and an understanding of how different GitLab implementations operate and affect customers.</li> <li>Demonstrated ability to learn, collaborate across teams, and apply transferable skills from related technical support or engineering roles.</li> <li>Fluent Korean language skills (required)</li> </ul> <h2><strong>About the team</strong></h2> <p>We're a globally distributed group of Support Engineers across the Americas, Europe, the Middle East, and Africa, and Asia-Pacific. We work asynchronously and stay connected through pairing sessions, one-on-one meetings, coffee chats, and Slack. We structure our shifts to support our personal lives while meeting customer needs. If you're excited about this role, please apply and allow our recruiters to assess your application.</p> <hr> <p><strong>Country Hiring Guidelines: </strong>GitLab hires new team members in countries around the world. Our Talent Acquisition team can help answer any questions about location after starting the recruiting process.  </p> <p><strong>Privacy Policy: </strong>Please review our <a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/hiring/candidate-faq/recruitment-privacy-policy/" target="_blank">Recruitment Privacy Policy.</a> Your privacy is important to us.</p> <p>GitLab is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace and is an affirmative action employer. GitLab will not tolerate discrimination or harassment based on any of these characteristics. title: Site Reliability Engineer, Infrastructure Platforms — AMER (Intermediate to Senior Staff)
description: <div class="content-intro"><p>GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.</p> <p>The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OuZIb5zszQI">Co-create the future with us</a> as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.</p> <p>*<em>Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><p><strong>An overview of this role</strong></p> <p>Site Reliability Engineers keep GitLab's user-facing services and production systems running reliably at scale. They combine software engineering with operational excellence, applying sound engineering principles, automation, and continuous improvement to build, operate, and evolve our production infrastructure.</p> <p>This is a single application for Site Reliability Engineering opportunities across Infrastructure Platforms. Rather than asking you to choose the right team or level upfront, we evaluate your skills holistically and match you to the opportunity that best aligns with your experience and our hiring needs. We hire Site Reliability Engineers from Intermediate through Senior Staff across multiple Infrastructure Platforms teams.</p> <p>We don't expect every candidate to have experience with every technology in our environment. We're looking for engineers with strong technical fundamentals, a growth mindset, and the ability to learn quickly. We'll support you in becoming successful with GitLab's tools, systems, and ways of working.</p> <p><strong><span style="text-decoration: underline;">Please note: This position is open to candidates based in the United States and Canada only. Candidates based in the United Kingdom can apply to this posting:</span> <a href="https://job-boards.greenhouse.io/gitlab/jobs/8773546002">Site Reliability Engineer, Infrastructure Platforms — UK (Intermediate to Senior Staff)</a></strong></p> <p><strong>How our SRE hiring works</strong></p> <p>Because this is a single application for SRE roles across Infrastructure Platforms, our process is built to evaluate you once and match you well, rather than interviewing separately for every team.</p> <ul> <li><strong>Recruiter Screen:</strong> A conversation about your background, what you're looking for, and the level and teams that fit, so we can point your process in the right direction.</li> <li><strong>Core Technical: </strong>The shared assessment every SRE candidate takes, regardless of eventual team. A low-stress, collaborative discussion covering system architecture and incident review.</li> <li><strong>Hiring Manager Interview: </strong>A conversation about ownership, judgment, execution, collaboration, and growth, the non-technical signals that make an SRE effective at GitLab.</li> <li><strong>Peer Technical: </strong>Team-specific depth, run by SREs from the team you're most likely to join, focused on the problems that team actually works on.</li> <li><strong>Skip-Level Interview: </strong>A conversation with a senior leader on values alignment, and how you'll work across teams.</li> </ul> <p>After your interviews, we consider your performance alongside our current hiring needs to confirm the level and team where you'll do your best work. Interview results are a major factor, and final placement also reflects our active hiring priorities at the time.</p> <p><strong>We’ll calibrate your level throughout the interview process based on the scope and impact of your experience.</strong></p> <ul> <li>Intermediate: You independently deliver meaningful reliability improvements within a defined area.</li> <li>Senior: You own complex reliability work end to end and raise the effectiveness of your team.</li> <li>Staff: You shape reliability across multiple teams, solving systemic problems and creating approaches others can reuse.</li> <li>Senior Staff: You set technical direction across a broader Infrastructure area and influence reliability strategy at organizational scale.</li> </ul> <p><strong>What you'll do</strong></p> <ul> <li>Keep user-facing services and production systems reliable, scalable, and efficient</li> <li>Build automation and tooling that reduces toil and replaces manual work with repeatable, infrastructure-as-code-driven workflows</li> <li>Operate and troubleshoot production systems on Kubernetes, including deployments, rollouts, and scaling</li> <li>Write and maintain infrastructure as code, and ship changes safely through CI/CD and GitOps</li> <li>Participate in on-call, triage alerts, follow and improve runbooks, and escalate appropriately</li> <li>Contribute to the observability stack, using metrics, logs, and SLOs to detect symptoms early rather than just outages</li> <li>Take part in incident response and post-incident reviews, turning learnings into changes in automation and process</li> <li>Document runbooks, architecture decisions, and reviews so your findings become repeatable practices</li> </ul> <p><strong>What you'll bring</strong></p> <ul> <li>Experience keeping production systems reliable, combining an operations mindset with real software engineering practice</li> <li>Experience building net-new infrastructure tooling and automation, not just configuring existing tools. For example, Terraform modules, Kubernetes operators or controllers, or production automation and services written from scratch</li> <li>The ability to read, debug, and reason about code. Most of our teams work in Go; some work in Ruby. You can discuss a piece of code's behavior, performance, and failure modes</li> <li>Experience with infrastructure as code, and with Kubernetes and its ecosystem, at a depth appropriate to your level</li> <li>Hands-on experience with at least one major cloud provider (GCP or AWS)</li> <li>Familiarity with observability practices, including metrics, logging, alerting, and SLOs or SLIs, and using data to inform operational decisions</li> <li>Comfort participating in on-call and incident response, with a structured approach to troubleshooting under pressure</li> <li>Strong written communication and the ability to operate as a manager-of-one in an async, distributed environment</li> <li>A track record of using automation, and increasingly AI, to reduce toil and improve how you and your team work</li> <li>Alignment with GitLab's values and a commitment to working in accordance with them</li> </ul> <p><strong>About the team</strong></p> <p><a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/engineering/infrastructure-platforms/">Infrastructure Platforms</a> is responsible for the availability, reliability, performance, and scalability of GitLab’s user-facing services, most notably <a href="http://GitLab.com" target="_blank">GitLab.com</a>. You will lead large, cross-cutting backend initiatives, drive our modular architecture strategy, and define the standards that let teams move faster without compromising quality, security, reliability, or operability.</p> <p>This is a technical leadership role that combines deep backend expertise, systems judgment, product judgment, and influence across organizational boundaries. You will work with Product, Frontend, Infrastructure, Security, Data, Engineering Managers, and engineers across product groups, bringing subject matter expertise, and you will do it without relying on formal authority.</p> <h2><strong>Why you’ll love this role</strong></h2> <ul> <li><strong>Leverage:</strong> Your work multiplies across teams. The platforms, standards, and architectural decisions you lead determine how quickly everyone else can ship.</li> <li><strong>Genuinely Hard Problems:</strong> You’ll lead the modernization of a large monolith toward modular, reusable, appropriately independent systems — at the scale of a platform used by millions of users.</li> <li><strong>Influence Without Bureaucracy:</strong> You’ll shape technical direction across teams through clear written proposals and decision records, and partner with Product and Engineering leadership on platform roadmap and investment trade-offs.</li> <li><strong>Frontier AI Work:</strong> You’ll lead adoption of AI-assisted and agentic engineering workflows and define the review, quality, security, and privacy guardrails that make them safe to rely on.</li> <li><strong>Autonomy:</strong> You’ll thrive in our remote-first, asynchronous organization, where clear written communication and self-direction are the pillars of success.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What you’ll do</strong></h2> <ul> <li><strong>Lead Cross-Cutting Initiatives:</strong> Lead the technical design and delivery of large backend initiatives that span teams, and identify and remove systemic bottlenecks across product and infrastructure groups.</li> <li><strong>Own Architecture Strategy:</strong> Drive modular backend, service, data, and platform architecture. Lead modernization of the monolith and legacy backends toward modular, reusable, and appropriately independently operated systems — while preventing fragmentation and service sprawl.</li> <li><strong>Set the Standards:</strong> Define and improve standards for APIs, contracts, compatibility, schema evolution, testing, security, performance, observability, operability, and maintainability — plus the build, test, deploy, release, rollback, and production-readiness practices needed to operate modular features safely.</li> <li><strong>Establish Shared Patterns:</strong> Create the patterns for dependency management, data ownership, eventing, failure isolation, service maturity, and operational documentation. Establish Go service patterns and Kubernetes operating practices where they matter to our production estate, and guide Rust adoption where it solves a real systems, security, performance, or supply-chain problem.</li> <li><strong>Own What You Build in Production:</strong> Take part in on-call and incident response for the systems your teams own, act as a technical escalation point during complex incidents, and turn what you learn into architectural and operational improvements that prevent recurrence.</li> <li><strong>Influence and Partner:</strong> Shape technical direction across teams without formal authority, and partner with Product and Engineering leadership on platform-level roadmap decisions and investment trade-offs.</li> <li><strong>Grow Engineers:</strong> Mentor Senior and Intermediate engineers, shepherd technical debt reduction and reusable patterns that improve throughput, and raise the technical capability of the wider team.</li> <li><strong>Lead AI Adoption:</strong> Lead team-level adoption of AI-assisted and agentic workflows, including the quality, security, privacy, and operational guardrails, and help engineers direct, validate, reject, and course-correct agent output.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What you’ll bring</strong></h2> <ul> <li><strong>Cross-Team Technical Leadership:</strong> A sustained record of technical leadership across more than one team or a broad product area.</li> <li><strong>Deep Architecture Experience:</strong> Deep backend architecture and production experience in complex applications, services, or platforms, including scaling or governing APIs, service platforms, data systems, modular monoliths, or shared backend components.</li> <li><strong>Modularization in Production:</strong> Experience modernizing a monolith or legacy backend architecture in production, and with modular architecture such as bounded contexts, package encapsulation, ports and adapters, service extraction, event-driven boundaries, or an equivalent approach.</li> <li><strong>Influence Without Authority:</strong> A strong ability to create alignment through clear written proposals and decision records, so decisions are documented, understood, and adopted without constant escalation.</li> <li><strong>Product Judgment:</strong> The ability to balance customer outcomes, delivery speed, technical health, reliability, and long-term platform investment.</li> <li><strong>Mentorship:</strong> Experience mentoring engineers and shaping standards through code review, documentation, and example.</li> <li><strong>Agentic AI Leadership:</strong> Production experience with AI-assisted or agentic engineering workflows, including the ability to evaluate and improve how a team adopts them.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>Helpful experience </strong></h2> <ul> <li>Go services and APIs at scale.</li> <li>Kubernetes and cloud-native operations, including deployment, scaling, observability, rollback, and production readiness.</li> <li>Rust adoption or production ownership for systems, security, performance, or platform components.</li> <li>Ruby/Rails modularization and large-monolith modernization.</li> title: Staff Backend Engineer, Architecture Engineering: Nonlinear Productivity
description: <div class="content-intro"><p>GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.</p> <p>The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OuZIb5zszQI">Co-create the future with us</a> as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.</p> <p>*<em>Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><h2><strong>An overview of this role</strong></h2> <p>As a Staff Engineer, you'll be the technical anchor for GitLab's Nonlinear Productivity team in the US: the person who decides what "proven" means before something ships, and who helps shape what the team builds next, not just how to build it. It's a from-scratch, generalist team with no dedicated product manager — that ownership starts on day one.</p> <p>Some examples of the problems this team takes on:</p> <ul> <li>Cutting the time it takes to complete a good code review — one that still keeps a human in the loop — by half, using agentic solutions.</li> <li>Turning a manual, error-prone release step into an agentic workflow that catches its own mistakes before a human ever has to.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What you'll do</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Set the technical direction for the team's agentic systems, from how agents are orchestrated to where a step should stay human-owned, and defend those calls once they're tested against real code.</li> <li>Discover and prioritize sources of friction across GitLab's SDLC, driving the fix — agentic, process-based, or both — from a rough hypothesis through to a shipped, measured result.</li> <li>Work across any part of GitLab's codebase as the problem requires, since this team operates like a small, generalist group rather than one scoped to a single service.</li> <li>Apply distributed systems judgment to catch cases where generated code looks correct but breaks under concurrency, at scale, or across deployment topologies (including self-managed, dedicated, and multi-tenant environments), and coach others to do the same.</li> <li>Mentor senior and mid-level engineers on agent engineering practices and distributed systems judgment, through design reviews and pairing that raise the team's collective bar rather than just your own output.</li> <li>Collaborate with the India-based group a few times a week to align on the roadmap, and represent the team's technical progress to stakeholders in the Chief Technology Officer's organization.</li> <li>Serve as a bar raiser for the team's hiring, owning the Technical Leadership round for other Staff-level candidates as the team scales.</li> <li>Own a greenfield technical foundation from day one, with your scope and impact free to grow as the team scales.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What you'll bring</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Experience building reliable agentic or large language model (LLM)-based systems, including multi-step orchestration, tool use, guardrails, and recovery.</li> <li>Ability to work autonomously in unfamiliar codebases and drive solutions from discovery through completion.</li> <li>Strong distributed systems and computer science fundamentals, including coordination, consistency, idempotency, rate limiting, failure modes, and degradation under load.</li> <li>Proficiency in Go, Rust, or Python, with the ability to read and modify code in the others.</li> <li>A track record of delivering results from unclear or incomplete requirements — able to take a complex, loosely specified problem and decompose it into a concrete proposal of small, shippable steps.</li> <li>Experience designing evaluation frameworks for systems where "looks plausible" and "is actually correct" are different questions, and a track record of raising the quality bar for a team's output, not just your own.</li> <li>A history of unblocking and enabling teammates — through design reviews, technical writing, or mentoring — and of engaging regularly with other teams to find where collaboration actually pays off.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>About the team</strong></h2> <p>Nonlinear Productivity — shortened internally to "NLP," with no relation to natural language processing — is one of GitLab's newest teams: a strategic incubation group that reports into AI Platform leadership under the direct sponsorship of the CTO. It's split into a US group (this role) and an India-based group working the same charter; the two sync on roadmap and tooling a few times a week but otherwise run day to day on their own. Solutions that prove out internally are the team's path to a monetized, customer-facing GitLab offering.</p> <p>It's a good fit for engineers who want technical ownership of something with no existing playbook, and a hand in defining a brand-new part of GitLab from its first commit.</p> <div class="c-message_actions__container c-message__actions"> </div> <div><span style="font-size: xx-small;"><span style="color: white;">Remote-Global</span></span></div><div class="content-pay-transparency"><div class="pay-input"><div class="description"><p><em>The base salary range for this role’s listed level is currently for residents of the United States only. title: Staff Backend Engineer, Database Automation (Go)
description: <div class="content-intro"><p>GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.</p> <p>The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><h2>An overview of this role</h2> <p>As a Senior or Staff Backend Engineer with the <a class="textLink" href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/engineering/data-engineering/database-excellence/">Database Excellence group</a>, you'll build and evolve database automation and PostgreSQL as a service capabilities for GitLab. The level will be determined during the hiring process. You'll use Go to automate the full lifecycle of PostgreSQL across GitLab's infrastructure, making database operations safer, more consistent, and easier to scale for databases that sit behind high-throughput, always-on internet services. You'll work closely with partner teams to shape how GitLab provisions and manages PostgreSQL in a fully remote, highly collaborative environment.</p> <p>Some examples of our projects:</p> <ul> <li value="1"><a class="textLink" href="https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/database-team/traffic-replay-poc">SQL Traffic Replay Tooling</a>, which validates upgrades and changes against real production workloads.</li> <li value="2"><a class="textLink" href="https://gitlab.com/groups/gitlab-org/database-team/backend/-/work_items/1">PostgreSQL as a Service Platform</a>, which provides standardized, automated provisioning and lifecycle management for internal product databases.</li> <li value="3"><a class="textLink" href="https://gitlab.com/groups/gitlab-com/gl-infra/data-access/dbo/-/work_items/75">PostgreSQL Major Version Upgrade Automation</a>, which supports safe, repeatable major upgrades at GitLab.com scale.</li> </ul> <h2>What you’ll do</h2> <ul> <li value="1">Design, build, and maintain Go-based automation that manages the full PostgreSQL lifecycle, including provisioning, configuration, upgrades, failover, scaling, and decommissioning, reducing reactive operational work that currently takes more than 80% of the team's time.</li> <li value="2">Build automation that works across infrastructure-as-code tooling and cloud infrastructure, and evaluate operator-based approaches as the platform evolves.</li> <li value="3">Use AI agents as a regular part of building and operating services, including implementation, review, and reducing repetitive work, while keeping the context agents need in the repository so the whole team can build on it.</li> <li value="4">Build for internet scale by designing automation and services for high-throughput, always-on production workloads, where GitLab.com traffic sets the bar for correctness, latency, and availability.</li> <li value="5">Integrate compute, storage, networking, identity and access management, and managed data services across cloud providers into one coherent PostgreSQL platform instead of creating bespoke setups for each database.</li> <li value="6">Build GitLab's PostgreSQL as a service platform to replace bespoke database setups with standardized, automated provisioning and lifecycle management, so supporting more databases doesn't require growing the operations team at the same rate.</li> <li value="7">Collaborate closely with product management, infrastructure, software delivery, and other engineering teams to design and ship high-performing solutions.</li> <li value="8">Research, design, and implement improvements to PostgreSQL performance, scalability, and data health, helping maintain more than 8 months of operational runway for all critical database saturation points.</li> <li value="9">Review database automation and Go changes from other engineers and contributors, with attention to safety, maintainability, and performance.</li> <li value="10">Document automation practices, PostgreSQL operational patterns, and guidance that helps engineers use and contribute to the platform.</li> <li value="11">Build safe, repeatable automation for PostgreSQL major version upgrades at GitLab.com scale, validating changes against real production traffic before rollout.</li> <li value="12">Operate what you build in production from end to end, using production feedback to guide each iteration.</li> </ul> <h2>What you’ll bring</h2> <ul> <li value="1">Professional software engineering experience working with PostgreSQL in large, complex production environments, including experience building or operating a database-as-a-service product.</li> <li value="2">Proficiency with Go, including designing, implementing, testing, and reviewing backend services.</li> <li value="3">Experience developing Kubernetes operators, controllers, or similar automation for the lifecycle of stateful services, especially databases. Kubernetes experience is one way to demonstrate this skill, but isn't required; comparable experience building database or infrastructure automation is welcome.</li> <li value="4">Comfort with infrastructure as code and core database operations concepts such as high availability, replication, backups, and system-level performance trade-offs.</li> <li value="5">Familiarity with Ruby is a plus but isn't required. Much of GitLab's application codebase uses Ruby on Rails, and being able to read it helps when designing automation that application teams depend on. We’ll expect you to become comfortable with it on the job, not on day one.</li> <li value="6">Strong written communication skills and comfort working asynchronously in an all-remote, distributed team.</li> <li value="7">Self-directed work style with effective organizational skills, the ability to manage priorities as a "manager of one," and alignment with GitLab's values of transparency, collaboration, inclusion, and open source contribution, as well as its <a class="textLink" href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/company/operating-principles/">operating principles</a>.</li> <li value="8">Ownership of the technical direction for a major initiative such as the PostgreSQL as a service platform, turning an ambiguous problem into an architecture and a sequenced plan that several engineers can execute in parallel.</li> <li value="9">Influence beyond the team, setting the patterns other engineers follow, partnering with sibling database, infrastructure, and platform teams, and growing engineers through design reviews and mentorship.</li> </ul> <h2>About the team</h2> <p>The <a class="textLink" href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/engineering/data-engineering/database-excellence/">Database Excellence group</a> keeps GitLab’s databases running reliably through proactive health management, operational excellence, and strategic enablement. We maintain operational runway by identifying and addressing saturation points, operate infrastructure through automated and scalable processes, and provide tools and frameworks that help teams build features sustainably. Our primary focus is GitLab.com, and we're expanding our scope to provide database health frameworks and tooling that benefit self-managed customers as well.</p><div class="content-pay-transparency"><div class="pay-input"><div class="description"><p><em>The base salary range for this role’s listed level is currently for residents of the United States only. description: <div class="content-intro"><p>GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.</p> <p>The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><h2>An overview of this role</h2> <p>The DAP Repository Flows team owns two areas within GitLab's Duo Agent Platform (DAP). The first is <strong>DAP onboarding</strong>, helping customers quickly set up a project so they can start using the Duo Agent Platform with minimal friction. The second is <strong>repository and background flows</strong>: autonomous and scheduled agents that work on a customer's codebase on their behalf.</p> <p>This work is central to how GitLab delivers AI-powered automation on repositories. As a Staff Software Engineer, you will set technical direction for the team, drive complex initiatives across team boundaries, and raise the engineering bar for how we build agentic experiences on top of the Duo Agent Platform.</p> <h2>What you'll do in this role</h2> <ul> <li>Set and drive the technical direction for the DAP Repository Flows team, making architecture decisions that shape how onboarding and repository/background flows are built.</li> <li>Lead the design and delivery of autonomous and scheduled agents that operate on customer codebases, building on top of the Duo Agent Platform.</li> <li>Design and refine the DAP onboarding experience so customers can get a project configured and productive quickly.</li> <li>Partner across teams in the broader DAP organization to align on interfaces, shared patterns, and platform capabilities.</li> <li>Mentor senior and intermediate engineers, review designs and code, and elevate the team's overall technical quality.</li> <li>Identify and resolve the hardest technical problems the team faces, and prevent them where possible through sound design.</li> <li>Contribute to a culture of autonomy, ownership, high context sharing, and async-first collaboration.</li> </ul> <h2>What we're looking for</h2> <ul> <li>Deep, hands-on experience with <strong>Ruby and Ruby on Rails</strong> in production systems.</li> <li>Demonstrated experience integrating <strong>LLMs into products</strong> (product integration, not ML model training).</li> <li>Experience building <strong>agentic systems</strong>: autonomous or semi-autonomous agents that take actions on a user's behalf.</li> <li>A track record of designing and shipping complex, high-scale systems and driving technical direction across teams.</li> <li>Strong written communication and the ability to operate effectively in a distributed, async-first environment.</li> <li>The judgment and influence expected of a staff-level engineer: setting direction, unblocking others, and multiplying the team's impact.</li> </ul> <h2>About the team</h2> <p>The DAP Repository Flows team is part of GitLab's broader Duo Agent Platform organization, within the AI/R&D group. These challenges may involve product gaps, performance degradation, scale bottlenecks, AI governance, adoption blockers, architectural constraints, Git usage patterns, continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) complexity, application programming interface (API) automation, security requirements, or operational instability.</p> <p>Forward Deployed Engineering provides technical stewardship in these moments. strategically important customers when adoption, retention, executive confidence, or public trust is materially at risk.</li> <li>Diagnose complex problems across GitLab product behavior, customer and agentic software development lifecycle</strong></h3> <ul> <li>Drive governed, measurable, and production-oriented adoption of GitLab Duo Agent Platform with strategic customers.</li> <li>Identify and resolve AI adoption blockers involving governance, usage controls, auditability, security, compliance, operating models, workflow design, and integrations.</li> <li>Develop customer-safe adoption patterns for the agentic software development lifecycle (SDLC), AI-assisted development, intent-based review, AI governance, and human-in-the-loop software delivery.</li> <li>Partner with Product, Engineering, Field, and Customer Success teams to turn AI adoption learning into reusable guidance and product improvements.</li> </ul> <h3><strong>Thought leadership</strong></h3> <ul> <li>Create technical narratives grounded in customer experience and product reality that can help shape the industry’s approach.</li> <li>Contribute to Well-Architected Frameworks, whitepapers, webinars, reference architectures, technical strategy memos, and adoption frameworks.</li> <li>Guide ideas through discovery, formulation, validation, amplification, and adoption across GitLab.</li> <li>Partner with SA, CSA, Product, Engineering, Marketing, Product Marketing Management, CSM, Support, and executive stakeholders to make technical thought leadership a shared company capability.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What you’ll bring</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Staff-level experience building, operating, or improving complex production software systems.</li> <li>Experience contributing to large, mature product codebases with high standards for testing, maintainability, performance, and security.</li> <li>Strong Ruby on Rails or Go experience and the ability to contribute directly to GitLab’s product and adjacent systems.</li> <li>Experience with AI-assisted software development, agentic workflows, AI governance, model evaluation, context management, prompt and workflow design, or AI adoption in enterprise environments.</li> <li>Experience diagnosing complex system behavior across application code, data stores, infrastructure, observability, networking, APIs, and customer usage patterns.</li> strategic customers or senior technical stakeholders in ambiguous, high-impact situations.</li> <li>The ability to coordinate across product, engineering, field, and customer teams without formal authority.</li> <li>Strong written communication and sound judgment, including the ability to create technical narratives and distinguish reusable product work from customer-specific customization.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>Strongly preferred qualifications</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Direct experience with GitLab as a platform, including GitLab.com, GitLab Dedicated, or GitLab architecture frameworks, requests for comments, public technical writing, or internal strategy documents.</li> <li>A background in performance engineering, site reliability engineering, platform engineering, infrastructure engineering, or distributed systems.</li> <li>Experience working in open source or highly asynchronous engineering environments.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>Technologies and domains</strong></h2> <p>Directly relevant technologies and domains include:</p> <ul> <li>Go, Rust or Python</li> <li>AI Engineering and Agentic SDLC</li> <li>PostgreSQL</li> <li>Redis and analysis</li> <li>Vue and TypeScript</li> <li>APIs and automation</li> <li>DevSecOps governance, security, and compliance</li> <li>Ruby on Rails</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What this role is This role reports to the Engineering Manager, Purchase.</p> <p><strong><strong class="textBold">Some examples of our projects:</strong></strong></p> <ul> <li value="1">Unifying separate purchase flows into one consistent purchase experience</li> <li value="2">Building and scaling GitLab Flex subscription flows that let customers reserve spend month to month across seats, artificial intelligence (AI) credits, Runners, and other GitLab capabilities without renegotiating their contract</li> <li value="3">Evolving self-service promotional discounts for existing and prospective customers</li> <li value="4">Modernizing the purchase frontend to improve clarity, accessibility, and conversion</li> <li value="5">Strengthening integrations between the purchase flow and downstream billing and CRM systems for accuracy and resilience</li> </ul> <h2>What you’ll do</h2> <ul> <li value="1">Design and build fullstack features across the purchase journey.</li> <li value="2">Lead technical design for new purchasing capabilities and the unified purchase experience.</li> <li value="3">Partner with Product and Design to turn purchasing requirements into resilient, well-tested technical solutions.</li> <li value="4">Ensure purchase flows integrate correctly and safely with downstream billing and CRM systems.</li> <li value="5">Set and uphold engineering standards for code quality, testing, rollout safety, and monitoring.</li> <li value="6">Mentor engineers and review merge requests with thoughtful, constructive feedback.</li> <li value="7">Identify and reduce technical debt and architectural risk in the purchase experience.</li> <li value="8">Participate in incident response for purchase-related issues because of their direct revenue impact.</li> </ul> <h2>What you’ll bring</h2> <ul> <li value="1">Professional fullstack engineering experience across frontend and backend code; Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><h4><strong>An overview of the role</strong></h4> <p>We are seeking a Staff Security Research Engineer to join our<a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/security/product-security/security-platforms-architecture/application-security/"> </a>Application Security Team to conduct cutting-edge security research on GitLab's AI-powered DevSecOps capabilities. As GitLab transforms software development through intelligent collaboration between developers and specialized AI agents, we need security researchers who can proactively identify and validate vulnerabilities before they impact our platform or customers.</p> <p>In this role, you'll be at the forefront of security research, working with our GitLab DevSecOps platform, Duo Agent Platform, GitLab Duo Chat, and AI workflows that represent the future of human/AI collaborative development. You'll develop novel testing methodologies (including for AI agent security), conduct hands-on penetration testing, and translate emerging threats into actionable security improvements. Your research will directly influence how we build and secure the next generation of AI-powered DevSecOps tools, ensuring GitLab remains the most secure software factory platform on the market.</p> <p>This position offers the unique opportunity to help shape security and AI security practices in one of the world's largest DevSecOps platforms, working with engineering teams who are pushing the boundaries of what's possible with AI-assisted software development. You'll have access to cutting-edge AI systems and the freedom to explore creative attack scenarios while contributing to the security of millions of developers worldwide.</p> <p>This role reports to the Senior Manager of Application Security </p> <h4><strong>What you'll do: </strong></h4> <ul> <li>Conduct security research in two or more specialty areas.</li> <li>Identify novel, systemic, and chained vulnerabilities in GitLab, where individual weaknesses combine for outsized impact.</li> <li>Validate security vulnerabilities through hands-on testing, developing proof-of-concept exploits that demonstrate real-world attack scenarios.</li> <li>Assess emerging industry vulnerability classes against the GitLab codebase in your areas of expertise, and drive remediation of the class rather than the instance.</li> <li>Conduct security research into GitLab's AI and agentic surfaces, and participate in defining the security requirements that engineering teams build against.</li> <li>Build the tooling and automation that scales security research, including agent-assisted vulnerability discovery across our codebase.</li> <li>Research the security posture of open source tools and dependencies integrated with GitLab, report findings to their maintainers, and track mitigation following our <a href="https://about.gitlab.com/security/disclosure/">responsible disclosure guidelines</a>.</li> <li>Solve technical problems of high scope, complexity, and ambiguity.</li> <li>Define and implement security technical and process improvements.</li> <li>Contribute to the team roadmap.</li> <li>Provide actionable and constructive feedback to the engineering teams that need to act on your findings.</li> <li>Mentor and advise other individual contributors within the team, and sometimes outside of it.</li> <li>Share knowledge and novel vulnerability types with the security community.</li> </ul> <h4><strong>What you'll bring</strong></h4> <ul> <li>7+ years of experience in security research, penetration testing, or offensive security roles</li> <li>Hands-on experience discovering and exploiting vulnerabilities.</li> <li>Be a subject matter expert (SME) of at least two technical areas impacting the security of the product.</li> <li>Proficiency in one or more of Ruby, Go, Python, TypeScript, or Rust. title: Strategic Account Executive, AI - San Francisco
description: <div class="content-intro"><p>GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.</p> <p>The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OuZIb5zszQI">Co-create the future with us</a> as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.</p> <p>*<em>Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><h3><strong>Location- San Francisco, California </strong></h3> <h3><strong>An overview of this role</strong></h3> <p>As a Strategic Account Executive for the San Francisco region, you'll drive GitLab's enterprise growth by helping some of the area's most influential organizations, including a concentrated focus on leading AI companies, adopt, implement, and expand their use of our AI-powered DevSecOps platform. You'll focus on enterprise accounts, with particular emphasis on foundation model labs, AI infrastructure providers, and applied AI companies scaling rapidly in the region, guiding customers through complex digital and DevSecOps transformations and driving pipeline generation that translates into measurable Net ARR and long-term expansion. In this role, you'll act as a key connector between customer stakeholders and GitLab's field organization so GitLab is seen as a trusted, long-term partner across the full sales cycle. In your first year, you'll be expected to build a strong enterprise portfolio across your territory, including a meaningful share of AI-native accounts, create repeatable sales motions, and consistently forecast and report on deal progress and account health.</p> <h3><strong>What you'll do</strong></h3> <ul> <li class="font-claude-response-body whitespace-normal break-words pl-2">Drive Development, Channel & Alliances, and other technical specialists to deliver transformative, AI-powered DevSecOps solutions tailored to the unique velocity and scale demands of AI-native engineering organizations.</li> <li class="font-claude-response-body whitespace-normal break-words pl-2">Shape the future of software development by crafting innovative solutions that align GitLab's platform with customers' long-term vision, compliance needs, and business objectives, including the specific infrastructure, security, and governance challenges AI companies face as they scale model development and deployment.</li> <li class="font-claude-response-body whitespace-normal break-words pl-2">Build deep, strategic partnerships by mastering your customers' industry landscape, success metrics, and growth trajectories, including a strong point of view on the AI/ML ecosystem, so you can position GitLab as their indispensable technology ally.</li> <li class="font-claude-response-body AI-driven development.</li> <li class="font-claude-response-body whitespace-normal break-words pl-2">Knowledge of San Francisco's enterprise and AI market, including key industries, buying centers, and decision-making dynamics, with the ability to build and nurture a relevant professional network.</li> <li class="font-claude-response-body whitespace-normal break-words pl-2">Ability to drive new negotiation, and closing.</li> <li value="4">Demonstrated skill in account planning, forecast management, and coordinating cross-functional resources across pre-sales, post-sales, and support.</li>
